title: Turnkey commercial fit-out: shop, salon, office — stages and budget
seo_title: Commercial Fit-Out in Kyiv: Stages and Budget
description: Turnkey commercial fit-out in Kyiv: shop, beauty salon, office. Stages of work, what drives the estimate, a sample budget calculation and common mistakes.
lead: A turnkey commercial fit-out has one goal — to get the business earning as early as possible and without rework. Here are the stages of fitting out a shop, beauty salon or office, what drives the estimate and how to calculate a budget at the start.
photo_alt: Stylist's station with an oval backlit mirror and a chair at Dolls beauty salon
body: How a commercial fit-out differs from a residential one

In an apartment you renovate for yourself, and the main questions are comfort and aesthetics. In commercial premises the space has to work for revenue: draw customers in from the street, guide them through the floor, let staff work efficiently and withstand a daily flow of people. Every decision — from flooring to lighting — is also judged by its effect on the business.

There are practical differences too. Commercial premises are more often leased, so landlord conditions and approvals matter. There are more building services: ventilation, high-capacity electrics, dedicated circuits for equipment, fire safety. And the schedule is tighter: every day of works is a day of rent without income.
the space works for sales and service, not just looks
materials are rated for heavy use
the schedule is tied to the opening date
Shop, salon, office: what matters in each
The stages are similar, but the priorities differ by format. They determine where to spend the budget and where you can save.
shop and showroom: shopfront and entrance, the customer route through the floor, product lighting, shelving and checkout, fitting rooms
beauty salon: stylist stations with sockets and lighting, wash basins and drainage, ventilation, sterilisation room, reception and waiting area
office: open-plan areas and meeting rooms, acoustics, low-voltage networks, kitchen, breakout area, toilets

In a beauty salon, for example, it is critical to position the stations in advance: sockets, lighting at each mirror and water to the basins all depend on it. Moving a basin after finishing means relaying the floor. In a shop, the shopfront and lighting come first: products must be visible from the street, and customers should flow through the floor without hitting dead ends.
Dolls beauty salon entrance with a black awning, a round sign and a ramp
Dolls Salon: the entrance — the first thing a client sees
survey of the premises: walls, floor slabs, building services, allocated power
brief: business format, equipment, number of workstations, opening date
interior design: layout, concept, working drawings, specification
estimate based on the design and works schedule
building services: electrics, ventilation, air conditioning, water, low-voltage systems
installation of lighting, sanitary ware, doors, signage

The most important rule: building services are completed before finishing and inspected against the drawings. Anything hidden in walls and ceilings is expensive to redo once closed. That is why concealed works are photographed before closing, and you see them in the reports.

The second principle is working in parallel. While rough works are under way, long-lead furniture, lighting and equipment are ordered. By the end of finishing everything is already on site rather than in transit.
Leases and approvals: what to clarify in advance

If the premises are leased, some decisions depend on the building owner rather than on you. Whether partitions can be changed, ventilation routed to the facade, signage installed or the power supply upgraded — all of this should be agreed in writing before works begin. Otherwise the design may need to be redone in the middle of the renovation.

Also agree on working hours: in business centres and residential buildings noisy works are often allowed only at certain times, and deliveries go through a separate entrance. These conditions affect the schedule, so we build them into the works plan from the start.
which layout changes the landlord allows
where outdoor AC units and signage can go
what power is allocated and whether it can be increased
when noisy works and deliveries are permitted
The cost of a commercial fit-out depends less on floor area than on the condition of the premises and the scope of building services. Two units of the same size can differ in cost many times over.
starting condition: bare concrete or old finishes to strip out
ventilation and air conditioning — especially for salons and food venues
electrics: capacity, number of circuits, sales floor lighting
Workstations with monitors by a green wall and a linear light fitting — Office Chicago
Breakout area with leather armchairs by a shelving unit — Office Chicago

Our confirmed rates: interior design from $30 per m² (minimum project fee $2,500), office renovation from $350 per m². Shops, salons and food venues are priced from the design, because the scope of building services varies widely.

Example for a 200 m² office: design from 200 × $30 = $6,000, renovation from 200 × $350 = $70,000. Total starting estimate — from $76,000, excluding furniture and equipment. For a small 60 m² salon, design at the rate would be 60 × $30 = $1,800, so the minimum project fee of $2,500 applies.

These are planning benchmarks, not a final price. The exact figure comes from the estimate after the survey and design. If CAS carries out the renovation to our design, the final cost stays within ±5% of the approved estimate. More about formats and prices on our [commercial renovation](/en/commercial-renovation) page.

Most of these mistakes happen because renovation, design and procurement are run by different people who do not see the whole picture. When design, estimate and works are in one pair of hands, such issues are caught at the drawing stage.

faq: How much does a commercial fit-out cost?
Office renovation starts from $350 per m², interior design from $30 per m² (minimum $2,500). Shops, salons and food venues are priced from the design, after a survey and brief.
Do I need a design project to fit out a shop or salon?
Yes. Without a design you cannot accurately place equipment, sockets, lighting and wet areas — and therefore cannot get an estimate without surprises.
Yes, if works run in parallel: furniture and equipment are ordered during rough works, not after finishing.
